Thirty-five comments

Eddie Moloney’s Favorite

I have seen this tune with various other names: Paddy Doorhy’s, The Drogheda Lasses, Mary of the Grove. Frankie Kennedy recorded a haunting and beautiful version of this with a slow air on one of the early Altan CD’s (Harvest Storm?). He plays it very slowly and with a strong “dotted” feeling, B2G>BE>BG etc. I knew it originally from Loesberg’s “An Irish Tunebook, Vol. 2” (Ossian), where it has different measures 4 and 8, and a different B part. I think it is one of those tunes that can be started slow and than speeded up with a very nice effect.

This reel has nothing to do with the title “Dobbin’s Flowery Vale” . Frankie learned the air of the song of that name from Robert Cinnamond, and stuck this reel after it. The only thing the 2 distinctly separate tunes have in common is that Frankie recorded them one after the other.

Early version

This tune appears in the Larry Smyth Manuscript c.1890-1920, under the title “The Drogheda Reel”. Smyth (d.1930) was from Abbeylara, Co. Longford. Josephine Keegan has published Smyth’s version in her book which she sourced through a Longford contact who in turn sourced from Fr. John Quinn, Gortletteragh Co. Leitrim, a proponent of local Longford and Leitrim music. He used this tune from the Smyth MS in one of his Ceili Bands of the 1970s .

Eddie Moloney’s Favourite, X:10

This version is transcribed from Eddie Moloney - Master Musician, disc 2, track 14, where he plays it on whistle.

It’s basically the same setting as the previous one, with a couple variations that I put in. On both instruments he jumps the octave, especially on the E and D in the A part pedal figures, but on the whistle he puts even more notes in the second octave. I didn’t transcribe every variation, but put in a few of those octave jumps in both transcriptions to give an indication of the types of things he’s doing. On the whistle track, he does a nice triplet in the B part, so I added that here.

Are we sure about this being a Paddy Doorhy composition?

Not to dispute the email that Jeremy received many moons ago but, as stated in a previous comment, this tune appears in a collection from the late 19th/early 20th century. Is anybody familiar with who Paddy Doorhy was? If it appears in that collection then Paddy must have been knocking around in the 19th century. AND, if his daughter, Delia Flannery was still alive and kicking 24 years ago, she’d have been of an advanced age. Plus, there are several versions of this tune. Cathal McConnell had a version of it which I posted a few years back and, I think, Micho Russell might have had another take on it?

Re: Eddie Moloney’s Favourite

OK, Paahto, you’ve got me intrigued here. A couple of points to raise, and a discovery.
1 - on the Eddie Moloney double CD referenced above with transcriptions by Nico, [ tune versions 9 and 10 ], the CD insert doesn’t mention Paddy Doorhy in relation to this tune, but follows the title “Eddie Moloney’s Favourite” with, in brackets, “Tommy Whelan’s #3”. Make of that as you will.
2 = I remembered that another famous Galway musician, Joe Burke, no less, had recorded this on his “Tailor’s Fancy” flute album, under the title “Paddy Doorhy’s”, and the sleeve notes have this to say :
“The second tune I got from Paddy Doorhy, a Leitrim Ceili Band colleague and a very good fiddler who comes from a place called Boston, near Loughrea, Co. Galway”.
3 - A “Google” on “Paddy Doorhy” came up with this :
